quote: We investigated the detailed clinical and genetic information of the gene-confirmed FCCM individuals, including the proband and family members. (Table 2) The family members of one patient with a KRIT1 variant (K7), and two patients with PDCD10 variants (P1 and P2), received genetic testing, and four family members with the same variant as the proband were detected. Furthermore, these family members had CCM lesions confirmed by brain MRI. Two patients (K3 and P2) had spinal CM, and one (C1) had cutaneous CM. Among the probands with mutations detected, six experienced CASH. Two patients experienced recurrent symptomatic hemorrhage and severe neurological sequelae. In the KRIT1 variant group, two patients (22.2%) had splice-site mutations, and the others had protein-truncating variants. (Table S1) All of the mutations were null. The CCM2 group comprised one patient with a nonsense mutation and one with a missense mutation. The PDCD10 group included one patient with a nonsense mutation and one with a splice-site mutation. Interestingly, five novel variants and one novel variant were confirmed in KRIT1 and PDCD10, respectively. Four patients with KRIT1 variants had a history of tumor or a current tumor. One patient (K3) presented with headache and neck pain. Brain and spine MRI demonstrated CCM and spinal CM. At the age of 52 years, a follow-up spine MRI revealed an increased size and prominent heterogeneous enhancement of T2 high signal intensity around the CM in the thoracic spinal cord. The neuroradiologist suggested the possibility of CM with a recent hemorrhage and tumorous condition. The surgical biopsy exhibited diffuse midline glioma, classified as WHO grade IV.

quote: Comparison of two receiver operating curves predicting the detection of CCM gene mutation. The prediction model for the detection of CCM gene mutations was derived from the presence of lesions at specific anatomical sites (brainstem, lateral temporal, and parietal lobe), which were associated with mutation detection. Subtracting the presence of brainstem lesions significantly reduced the area under the curve. B: brainstem, LT: lateral temporal lobe, P: parietal lobe, AUC: area under the curve, CCM: cerebral cavernous malformation.
